articles.title: The Friends You Outgrow (And the Guilt That Follows)
articles.titleHinglish: Wo Dost Jinse Aap Aage Nikal Jaate Ho
articles.content:
Nobody warns you that some friendships end without a fight. There is no betrayal, no dramatic last message. You simply notice that you have nothing to say, that the meeting is being scheduled out of duty, and that you feel slightly tired afterwards.

Then comes the guilt, usually with the same sentence attached: he was there for me in school.

He was. That is true and it will stay true. But friendship is not a debt that must be serviced forever. People change at different speeds and in different directions, and two people who fit perfectly at nineteen can genuinely have nothing in common at twenty-nine. This is not treachery. It is arithmetic.

It helps to notice what actually holds most friendships together. Not shared values, usually — shared circumstances. The same class, the same office, the same neighbourhood, the same daily boredom. Remove the circumstance and many friendships have nothing underneath, which is why they fade after a job change or a move even when nobody did anything wrong.

There are two versions of outgrowing, and they should be handled differently.

The first is drift. Nothing is bad, there is just less in common. This one does not need surgery. Let it become what it is — the friend you meet twice a year, warmly, with no expectation of more. Some of the best relationships of adult life are these low-frequency, high-affection ones. Trying to force them back to daily contact is what makes them feel like work.

The second is different: the friendship that has become corrosive. The jokes that have an edge. The person who is noticeably happier when things go badly for you. The one who mocks whatever you are trying to build. That is not drift, and it does not fix itself with distance alone. You can love a person's history and still decide the present version is not good for you.

A fair test before deciding anything: how do you feel in the hour after seeing them? Not during — during is easy, habit is comfortable. The hour after tells you the truth. Lighter or heavier? More yourself or slightly diminished?

And let yourself keep the good part. You do not have to rewrite the friendship as fake in order to justify letting it fade. Two things can be true — they were genuinely important to you then, and they are not part of your life now. Most endings are not betrayals. They are just seasons finishing, and the guilt you feel is usually a sign that you loved them, not a sign that you are doing something wrong.
articles.contentHinglish:
Koi nahi batata ki kuch dostiyan bina jhagde ke khatam hoti hain. Na dhokha, na koi dramatic aakhri message. Bas ek din notice hota hai ki baat karne ko kuch hai hi nahi, milne ka plan farz nibhaane ke liye ban raha hai, aur milne ke baad halki thakan mehsoos hoti hai.

Phir guilt aati hai, aksar isi line ke saath: school mein wo mere saath khada tha.

Tha. Yeh sach hai aur sach hi rahega. Par dosti koi karza nahi hai jise hamesha bharte rehna pade. Log alag raftaar aur alag disha mein badalte hain, aur unnees saal ki umar mein perfect fit do log unnatis mein sach mein bilkul alag ho sakte hain. Yeh gaddaari nahi hai. Yeh hisaab hai.

Yeh dekhna kaam ka hai ki zyadatar dostiyon ko jodta kya hai. Aksar values nahi — haalat. Ek hi class, ek hi office, ek hi mohalla, ek jaisa rozana ka boredom. Haalat hataao aur bahut si dostiyon ke neeche kuch nahi bachta, isiliye job badalne ya sheher badalne par wo dheere dheere khatam ho jaati hain, bina kisi ki galti ke.

Aage nikalne ke do version hote hain, aur dono ko alag tareeke se sambhaalna chahiye.

Pehla hai drift. Kuch bura nahi hai, bas common cheezein kam ho gayi hain. Iska operation zaroori nahi. Ise wahi ban jaane do jo hai — wo dost jisse aap saal mein do baar milte ho, garmjoshi se, bina zyada ummeed ke. Badi umar ki kuch behtareen dostiyan yahi kam frequency wali, zyada pyaar wali hoti hain. Inhe zabardasti rozana wale level par kheenchna hi unhe kaam jaisa bana deta hai.

Doosra alag hai: wo dosti jo gala rahi hai. Wo mazaak jinme dhaar hai. Wo insaan jo aapka bura hone par thoda zyada khush dikhta hai. Wo jo aapki har nayi koshish ka mazaak udaata hai. Yeh drift nahi hai, aur yeh sirf doori se theek nahi hota. Aap kisi ke ateet se pyaar kar sakte ho aur phir bhi tay kar sakte ho ki uska aaj wala version aapke liye theek nahi hai.

Kuch bhi tay karne se pehle ek imaandaar test: unse milne ke ek ghante baad kaisa lagta hai? Milte waqt nahi — us waqt to aasaan hai, aadat aaram deti hai. Baad ka ek ghanta sach batata hai. Halka ya bhaari? Zyada apne jaisa ya thoda chhota?

Aur achha hissa apne paas rakho. Dosti ko fake batana zaroori nahi hai sirf isliye ki use dheere dheere jaane dena justify ho jaaye. Do baatein sach ho sakti hain — wo us waqt sach mein zaroori the, aur ab wo aapki zindagi ka hissa nahi hain. Zyadatar ant dhokhe nahi hote. Wo mausam ka khatam hona hote hain, aur jo guilt aap mehsoos karte ho wo aksar iska nishaan hai ki aapne pyaar kiya tha, na ki iska ki aap galat kar rahe ho.

articles.title: The Friend Who Is Quietly Competing With You
articles.titleHinglish: Wo Dost Jo Chupke Se Aapse Compete Kar Raha Hai
articles.content:
You tell him you got the job. There is a half-second pause, then: that is good, though I heard that company has issues. You tell her about the trip. She tells you about a better one. Nothing that could be called an insult, but you leave every conversation feeling slightly flattened, and you cannot explain why.

Competitive friendship is hard to name because every individual instance is deniable. Reported to a third person, it sounds like nothing. He said congratulations. She just mentioned her trip. The pattern only exists across months, which is exactly why you doubt yourself.

A few reliable signatures.

The qualified congratulation. Good news is acknowledged and then immediately given a small wound. That is great — surprising, considering how the interview went.

The topic return. Every story you tell becomes a doorway back to them. It is not that they lack interest in you; it is that any spotlight in the room has to be redirected.

Enthusiasm that inverts. They are most warm and available when things are going badly for you, and strangely distant during your good weeks. This one is worth watching closely, because it can masquerade as loyalty for years.

And the public downgrade. In a group, they are the one who mentions your old failure as a joke. The joke is funny. It also happens to be load-bearing.

Why do people do this? Almost never out of hatred. Competitive friends are usually deeply insecure and have quietly decided that you are their measuring stick. Your progress does not read to them as your progress; it reads as their falling behind. Understanding this makes it less personal, and it does not make it less draining.

What helps is not confrontation, at least not first. Try controlling the supply. Stop bringing your good news to that friend. This sounds sad, and it is, but it is also clarifying — notice how much of the friendship remains when you are not offering material. Sometimes a great deal remains, and the competition was a small flaw in a good person. Sometimes almost nothing remains, and you have your answer.

If you do want to raise it, raise a specific instance rather than a diagnosis. Do not say you are competitive with me. Say: when I told you about the job, the first thing you said was about the company's problems. That landed badly. A specific moment can be discussed. A label can only be denied.

And examine your own reflexes while you are at it. Most of us have done this at least once — the friend who announced something good on a day we felt like a failure, and the small deflating sentence that came out before we could stop it. Noticing it in yourself is uncomfortable and useful, because the cure is the same in both directions: be genuinely happy out loud when someone you love wins. It costs nothing, and it is rarer than it should be.
articles.contentHinglish:
Aap use batate ho ki job lag gayi. Aadhe second ka pause, phir: achha hai, waise maine suna hai us company mein dikkatein hain. Aap use trip ke baare mein batate ho. Wo aapko usse behtar trip batati hai. Aisa kuch nahi jise insult keh sako, par har baat ke baad aap thoda dabe hue mehsoos karte ho, aur wajah samajh nahi aati.

Competitive dosti ka naam lena mushkil hai kyunki har ek waqia alag se deniable hota hai. Kisi teesre ko batao to kuch bhi nahi lagta. Usne to badhai di thi. Usne bas apni trip ka zikr kiya tha. Pattern sirf mahino mein banta hai, isiliye aap khud par shak karte ho.

Kuch pakki nishaaniyan.

Shart wali badhai. Achhi khabar maani jaati hai aur turant usme ek chhota sa cheera lagta hai. Bahut badhiya — waise interview jaisa gaya tha, tab to hairani hai.

Topic ki wapsi. Aapki har kahani unke paas laut jaane ka darwaza ban jaati hai. Baat yeh nahi ki unhe aapme dilchaspi nahi; baat yeh hai ki kamre ki roshni kahin bhi pade, use mod dena zaroori hai.

Ulta josh. Wo sabse garmjosh aur available tab hote hain jab aapka bura chal raha ho, aur aapke achhe hafton mein ajeeb tarah se door. Is par khaas nazar rakhni chahiye, kyunki yeh saalon tak wafadari ka bhes badal kar rehta hai.

Aur public downgrade. Group mein wahi hote hain jo aapki purani asafalta ka zikr mazaak ki tarah karte hain. Mazaak funny hota hai. Aur usi par poora bojh bhi tika hota hai.

Log aisa karte kyun hain? Lagbhag kabhi nafrat se nahi. Competitive dost aksar bahut insecure hote hain aur unhone chupchaap aapko apna paimana bana liya hota hai. Aapki tarakki unhe aapki tarakki nahi lagti; unhe apna peeche chhootna lagti hai. Yeh samajhne se baat kam personal ho jaati hai, par thakaan kam nahi hoti.

Madad confrontation se nahi hoti, kam se kam pehle to nahi. Supply control karke dekho. Us dost ko apni achhi khabar dena band karo. Yeh dukhi karne wala lagta hai, hai bhi, par isse saaf bhi hota hai — dekho ki material dena band karne par dosti mein kitna bacha rehta hai. Kabhi bahut kuch bacha rehta hai, aur competition ek achhe insaan ki ek chhoti kharabi thi. Kabhi lagbhag kuch nahi bachta, aur aapko jawab mil jaata hai.

Agar baat karni hi hai to diagnosis nahi, specific waqia uthao. Yeh mat kaho ki tum mujhse compete karte ho. Yeh kaho: jab maine job ki baat batayi, tumne sabse pehle company ki dikkatein bola. Wo achha nahi laga. Ek specific lamhe par baat ho sakti hai. Label par sirf inkaar hota hai.

Aur is beech apne reflex bhi check karo. Hum mein se zyadatar ne kabhi na kabhi yeh kiya hai — jis din khud ko fail mehsoos kar rahe the, us din kisi dost ne achhi khabar sunayi aur muh se ek chhoti si hawa nikaalne wali line nikal gayi. Khud mein use pehchaan lena uncomfortable bhi hai aur kaam ka bhi, kyunki dawa dono taraf ek hi hai: jab apna koi jeete to khul ke, awaaz mein khush ho jao. Kuch kharcha nahi hota, aur yeh jitna hona chahiye utna hota nahi.

articles.title: Why Making Friends Gets Harder After 25
articles.titleHinglish: 25 Ke Baad Dost Banana Mushkil Kyun Ho Jaata Hai
articles.content:
You have colleagues you like, a group chat that is mostly forwards, and nobody you could call at 2am. This is one of the most common experiences of adult life and one of the least discussed, because admitting it feels like admitting a defect.

It is not a defect. It is logistics.

School and college friendships were manufactured by three conditions that almost never occur again: repeated unplanned contact, large amounts of unstructured time, and shared vulnerability. You saw the same people daily without arranging it, you had hours to waste together, and you were all equally lost. Adult life removes all three. Meetings replace loitering, calendars replace spontaneity, and everyone performs competence.

Once you see it as a structural problem, the solutions become obvious and slightly boring — which is a good sign, because it means they work.

Repetition beats intensity. One brilliant conversation with someone you never see again produces nothing. A mediocre badminton game every Tuesday for four months produces a friend. Friendship is mostly a function of hours in proximity, so choose things that repeat automatically: a class, a sport, a weekly practice, the same gym slot. Do not look for the perfect group. Look for the recurring one.

Be the one who invites. Most adults are waiting to be invited, which is why so many lonely people are standing next to each other. The person willing to send the message — no matter how awkward — gets the friendships. Yes, some invitations go nowhere. That is the cost, and it is low.

Be specific. Let us catch up sometime is a polite way of never meeting. Are you free Saturday at 6, there is a place near your office produces an actual answer, either way.

And go slightly first on honesty. Closeness is built by small, well-timed admissions — I have been struggling with work lately — which give the other person permission to stop performing. Not everything at once; that is its own problem. Just a little more truth than the situation requires.

One more thing worth saying to the people who need to hear it. If you moved cities, or left a job, or came out of a long relationship, and your social life collapsed — nothing is wrong with you. Your friendships were built on a structure that no longer exists, and you are now doing manually what circumstance used to do for you. It is slower. It works. And the friendships you build this way, on purpose, in your thirties, are frequently better than the ones you inherited from proximity at nineteen.
articles.contentHinglish:
Aapke paas colleagues hain jo achhe lagte hain, ek group chat hai jisme zyadatar forwards hain, aur koi nahi hai jise raat do baje call kar sako. Yeh badi umar ki sabse aam experiences mein se ek hai aur sabse kam baat ki jaane wali, kyunki ise maan lena kisi kami ko maan lene jaisa lagta hai.

Yeh kami nahi hai. Yeh logistics hai.

School aur college ki dostiyan teen shartein banati thi jo phir kabhi lagbhag nahi banti: bina plan ke baar baar milna, khaali waqt ka dher, aur ek jaisi kamzori. Aap rozana bina arrange kiye ek hi logon se milte the, saath waqt barbaad karne ke ghante the, aur sab barabar ke khoye hue the. Badi umar teeno hata deti hai. Meetings ne bina matlab ghoomna kha liya, calendar ne spontaneity, aur ab sab kaabiliyat ka performance karte hain.

Jaise hi ise structure ki problem maan lo, hal saaf aur thode boring ho jaate hain — jo achhi nishaani hai, kyunki iska matlab hai wo kaam karte hain.

Dohraav intensity se jeetta hai. Kisi ke saath ek zabardast baat jiske baad dobara mile hi nahi — kuch nahi banta. Har Tuesday chaar mahine tak ek average badminton game — dost ban jaata hai. Dosti zyadatar paas bitaaye ghanton ka natija hai, isliye wo cheezein chuno jo apne aap repeat hoti hain: koi class, koi sport, koi weekly practice, gym ka wahi slot. Perfect group mat dhoondho. Repeat hone wala dhoondho.

Bulane wale khud bano. Zyadatar bade log bulaye jaane ka intezaar karte hain, isliye itne saare akele log ek doosre ke bagal mein khade hain. Jo message bhejne ki himmat karta hai — chahe kitna hi awkward lage — dostiyan usko milti hain. Haan, kuch invitations bekaar jaayenge. Wahi keemat hai, aur wo kam hai.

Specific bano. "Kabhi milte hain" kabhi na milne ka shishtachari tareeka hai. "Saturday shaam 6 baje free ho? Tumhare office ke paas ek jagah hai" — iska jawab milta hai, kuch bhi ho.

Aur imaandaari mein thoda pehle chalo. Nazdeeki chhoti, sahi waqt par ki gayi baaton se banti hai — kaam ko lekar aajkal mushkil chal rahi hai — jisse saamne wale ko performance band karne ki ijazat mil jaati hai. Sab kuch ek saath nahi; wo apni alag problem hai. Bas halka sa zyada sach jitna maahaul maang raha ho.

Ek aakhri baat un logon ke liye jinhe iski zaroorat hai. Agar aapne sheher badla, job chhodi, ya lambe rishte se bahar aaye, aur aapki social life beth gayi — aapme kuch galat nahi hai. Aapki dostiyan us structure par khadi thi jo ab hai hi nahi, aur ab aap haath se wo kaam kar rahe ho jo pehle haalat khud kar deti thi. Yeh dheema hai. Chalta hai. Aur jo dostiyan aap tees ki umar mein jaan bujh kar banate ho, wo aksar unnees ki umar mein nazdeeki se mil gayi dostiyon se behtar hoti hain.
